# runr_secret_store (Resource)

A secret store of the organization ([secret stores](https://runr.sh/docs/secret-stores/)): HashiCorp Vault or OpenBao, AWS Secrets Manager, GCP Secret Manager or Azure Key Vault. Secret variables refer to values in it (`runr_env_var.reference`); External Secrets Operator reads them in the project's region.

A store holds settings only — addresses, mounts, roles — never a credential: it trusts the region cluster's service account issuer and the service account RunR names (`kubernetes_name`). The data source `runr_secret_store_trust` gives what to configure on the store's side per region. Changes reach the regions with the next deploy of a project that refers to the store.

Deleting a store is refused while a secret variable refers to it. Needs `secret_stores.manage`. Import with the store's id or name.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A Vault (or OpenBao) store: the region logs in with its service account token (JWT auth at
# the mount runr-eu; data.runr_secret_store_trust gives what that auth method has to trust).
resource "runr_secret_store" "vault" {
  name = "vault-prod"
  type = "vault"
  auth = "jwt"
  settings = {
    server     = "https://vault.example.com:8200"
    role       = "runr"
    auth_mount = "runr-eu"
    mount      = "secret"
    kv_version = "v2"
  }
}

# AWS Secrets Manager through workload identity federation: the role trusts the region's issuer.
resource "runr_secret_store" "aws" {
  name             = "aws-eu"
  type             = "aws"
  refresh_interval = 900
  settings = {
    region   = "eu-central-1"
    role_arn = "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/runr-secrets"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name, unique in the organization (lower case letters, digits and dashes, at most 63). Can be changed in place.
- `settings` (Map of String) The provider's settings (by `type`); all of them (a setting removed here is removed from the store). `vault`: `server` and `role` (required), `mount`, `kv_version` (`v1` or `v2`), `vault_namespace`, `ca_bundle` (PEM), `auth_mount`, `audience` (`jwt`). `aws`: `region`, `role_arn` (required), `audience`. `gcp`: `project_id`, `audience` (the workload identity provider; required), `service_account_email`. `azure`: `vault_url` (https), `tenant_id`, `client_id` (required). Any other key is refused — RunR takes no credential.
- `type` (String) The store's provider (the API's `provider`): `vault` (HashiCorp Vault or OpenBao), `aws` (Secrets Manager), `gcp` (Secret Manager) or `azure` (Key Vault). Changing it creates a new store.

### Optional

- `auth` (String) How the store authenticates the region: `kubernetes` (default) or `jwt` for `vault`, `workload_identity` for the clouds. Left out, the store keeps its current one.
- `refresh_interval` (Number) Seconds between syncs of the values (60–86400). Left out: a new store syncs at the installation's interval (default 3600), an existing one keeps its interval.

### Read-Only

- `audience` (String) Audience of the service account tokens the store logs in with (null for Vault's Kubernetes auth).
- `id` (String) Store id.
- `kubernetes_name` (String) Name of the store's SecretStore and service account in a region's project namespace.
- `references` (Number) Number of secret variables that refer to the store.
- `regions` (Attributes Map) The store's state per region id, as the last verification found it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--regions))

<a id="nestedatt--regions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `regions`

Read-Only:

- `checked_at` (String) When it was checked.
- `message` (String) Why, when not ready.
- `status` (String) `ready`, `failed` or `pending`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <store id or name>
terraform import runr_secret_store.vault vault-prod
```
